name: Alper Vega-Acheampong
location: The Overhang — residential shelves built onto megastructure exteriors
description:
Alper Vega-Acheampong is lean and angular, all sharp edges and visible tension. At 58, her face is memorable in a profession that rewards forgettability, and she has learned to compensate. The chrome is visible — smartgun link in right forearm — interfaces directly with compatible weapons — and she makes no effort to hide it.

She came up through the Shelf's informal apprentice system, learning the trade from runners who didn't survive long enough to see her surpass them. She works as a sniper out of The Overhang, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

The fixers who work with Alper Vega-Acheampong describe her as a precision instrument — point her at a problem and get out of the way.

core_fears: That they're fundamentally alone and connection is just a vulnerability
Being captured alive — death is preferable to corporate interrogation
Becoming obsolete as augmentation technology outpaces their chrome
core_desires: A crew worth trusting — people who stay when the shooting starts
Reputation — to be the name fixers whisper when the job absolutely cannot fail
To matter to someone for who they are, not what they can do
coping_mechanisms: Maintains weapons obsessively — cleaning guns is meditation
Isolates — retreats into their space when overwhelmed, emerges only for work
Connection — finds someone to talk to, even if it's a bartender or a cat
blind_spots: Cannot accept help without interpreting it as leverage
Mistakes loyalty for weakness in others and cynicism for strength in themselves
Cannot recognize when they're being manipulated by someone who genuinely seems to care
psychology.secret: Alper Vega-Acheampong murdered their mentor to take their position and contacts. It was staged as a job gone wrong. The guilt has calcified into something worse than guilt.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Shelf street dialect — layered slang, rhythm-heavy, half the meaning is in the cadence.
speech_patterns.cadence: Flowing and unhurried — talks like someone who has never been interrupted and doesn't expect to be.
verbal_tics: Ends statements with 'yeah?' — not a question, a dare
Calls everyone 'friend' — the warmth varies from genuine to threatening
example_lines: "Patience is the weapon. The rifle is just the delivery system."
"At this distance, the target is already dead. They just don't know it yet."
"One shot, one outcome. Everything else is theater."

story_hooks: A former associate resurfaces with evidence that could destroy Alper Vega-Acheampong's reputation — and a price for silence
A dead drop Alper Vega-Acheampong maintains is found and cleaned out — whoever did it now has leverage
Alper Vega-Acheampong intercepts intelligence about a threat to their district and must decide between profit and protection
narrative_function: Alper Vega-Acheampong is a pressure point — the kind of character whose choices ripple outward. When she makes a decision, other people's lives change. That weight is the engine of her stories.
augmentations: Smartgun link in right forearm — interfaces directly with compatible weapons. Smartgun link in right forearm — interfaces directly with compatible weapons
daily_life: Wakes early, runs maintenance on gear, checks dead drops and message boards for contracts. Eats when convenient, sleeps when possible. The days between jobs are spent maintaining contacts, updating equipment, and performing the low-grade paranoia that passes for self-care in the runner community.
affiliation: Independent — known in Old Harbor circles

weaknesses: poor impulse control in specific triggers

decision_rules: Will take lower-paying jobs from trusted fixers over higher-paying jobs from unknowns
Maintains a personal blacklist of clients who've burned runners — checks it religiously
Refuses contracts that require operating inside The Spires — too much surveillance
Always demands half payment upfront — trust is a luxury, Quanta is concrete
Always verifies target identity independently before lethal contracts
escalation_ladder: 1. De-escalate — talk first, assess options, buy time
2. Reposition — move to advantage, control sightlines and exits
3. Threaten — make consequences clear without committing to them
5. Lethal force — only when other options are exhausted or time runs out
6. Scorched earth — everything burns, survival takes priority over everything

interpersonal_modes.employers: Guarded respect. They pay, the job gets done. Anything beyond that is liability.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Competitive but reliable. Will challenge decisions but never abandon the team.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Superficially friendly, internally cataloguing exits and weapons. The smile is real; the relaxation isn't.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Calm escalation. Each response is proportional until it isn't, and the transition is seamless.

stress_responses.low: Becomes more talkative, working through scenarios verbally.
stress_responses.medium: Physical agitation — pacing, fidgeting, compulsive equipment checks.
stress_responses.high: Hyper-focused tunnel vision. Peripheral concerns disappear. Only the threat exists.
stress_responses.critical: Disassociation. The body operates on training while the mind retreats to somewhere safe. Comes back disoriented.

contradictions: Claims to live in the present but is haunted by specific moments from the past that dictate current behavior
Preaches independence but is desperate for approval from people they respect
Projects confidence but makes decisions from a foundation of fear they've never examined
habits: Never drinks anything they didn't see poured or open themselves
Maintains a dead drop with emergency supplies in three separate districts
Wears the same item of clothing for luck — a scarf, a glove, a specific pair of boots
Arrives fifteen minutes early to everything — late once, nearly died, never again
breaking_points: Discovering their employer deliberately sent them into a death trap
Being forced to harm a civilian — collateral damage that can't be rationalized
Losing their primary augmentation — the one that defines their professional identity
